title: Best Before / Use By Date Declared (where applicable)
description: Detect whether a 'best before' or 'use by' date is declared on the package, as required by Rule 6(1)(da) for commodities that may become unfit for human consumption after a period of time. This rule is applicability-aware: it only applies when there is evidence the product is a perishable or time-sensitive commodity. For non-perishable products, this rule returns NOT_APPLICABLE and does not affect the screening score.
rule_reference: Rule 6(1)(da), Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 (inserted by G.S.R. 629(E), 23 June 2017)
amendment_status: Inserted by G.S.R. 629(E), 23 June 2017. Not further amended.
applicable_scope: Pre-packaged commodities which may become unfit for human consumption after a period of time. Not applicable to non-perishable goods.
conditions: Applies only when the product is identified as a perishable or time-sensitive commodity

detection_method.description: The system first determines whether the product is likely perishable or time-sensitive using food/beverage/perishable indicators. If applicability is established, it searches for best-before or use-by date declarations. If applicability cannot be established, the rule returns NOT_APPLICABLE.

validation_logic.pass_criteria: When applicable (product is perishable/time-sensitive), a best-before or use-by date declaration is found on the label.

evaluate.action: Check for applicability: search for food/beverage/perishable indicators (applicability_patterns). If found, product is likely perishable → rule is applicable. If not found, rule is NOT_APPLICABLE.
If applicable: search for best-before/use-by date patterns. If found → DETECTED. If keyword found but no date → UNCERTAIN. If nothing found → NOT_DETECTED.

observable_evidence.description: What the software can observe: text containing 'Best Before', 'Use By', 'Expiry', or similar date-related declarations, along with a date value. For applicability, food/beverage/perishable keywords indicate the product may require a best-before declaration.
examples: Text 'Best Before: 12 Months from Date of Manufacture' detected
Text 'Shelf Life: 18 months from packing' detected

status_values.DETECTED: The product is identified as perishable/time-sensitive, and a best-before/use-by declaration was found.
status_values.NOT_DETECTED: The product is identified as perishable/time-sensitive, but no best-before/use-by declaration was found.
status_values.UNCERTAIN: Applicability is uncertain, or date keyword found but date value unclear.
status_values.NOT_APPLICABLE: No evidence of perishable/time-sensitive product category. The product appears to be non-perishable.

cannot_conclude: Whether the best-before date satisfies the specific requirements for this product category
Whether the date format is legally sufficient
Whether the product falls under other laws (FSSAI, Drugs and Cosmetics) that may have their own date requirements
notes: Rule 6(1)(da): 'If a package contains a commodity which may become unfit for human consumption after a period of time, the best before or use by the date, month and year shall also be mentioned on the label.'
This rule is applicability-aware: missing best-before on a non-perishable product (e.g., steel utensils, electronics) is NOT a violation.
The system uses food/beverage/perishable keywords as a proxy for applicability. This is a heuristic.
Food products may follow FSSAI date labeling rules instead of LMPC Rule 6(1)(da).
limitations: Applicability detection relies on food/beverage keywords in OCR text. Some perishable products (e.g., certain cosmetics, medicines) may not have these keywords visible.
Date extraction from OCR may be imprecise due to formatting variations.
The system cannot verify that the best-before period is reasonable for the product type.
Products under other regulatory frameworks (FSSAI, CDSCO) may have different date labeling requirements.
